definitions.meaning: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a signal rocket like a Very light flare, and a deep brownish-crimson hue.

clue.text: I'm coming up with new tunes for dances

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word I'm is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of tunes are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A composer announces arrival with fresh melodies written for a ballroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns IM into MI in this down light; 'new' rearranges TUNES into NUETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuets are stately old court dances in triple time.

clue.text: US president to resolve New Deal

indicators.note: a new deal of cards is a reshuffle, so the letters of to resolve are dealt out again in another order

explanation.surface: A president pledges to sort out the country's troubles with his famous recovery programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Deal was the actual programme of the president in question, so the indicator doubles as scenery; as a card deal it reshuffles TO RESOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin and Theodore were both American heads of state with this surname.

clue.text: Unsealed circular letter to writer and editor

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone tears open a round-robin letter addressed to an author and the journal's editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsealed has been broken open, so it is open now.

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of lost nail come out in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A horse goes lame after a farrier's nail falls out of its shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male of the equine kind.

definitions.meaning: a teardrop, a single drop of water from the eye
a rip or split in fabric

explanation.definitionFit: One spelling covers a drop wept from the eye and a rip in cloth, though the two are said differently.

parts.note: read noted as set to musical notes: the book of words for an opera, rather than a famous school textbook

explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written words of an opera, published as a small book to go with the score.

clue.text: Flower head of hydrangea comes from Ireland

parts.note: the iris is a garden flower

indicators.note: head of signals taking only the opening letter of the word hydrangea

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a particular bloom on the hydrangea originated across the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is the adjective for things originating in Ireland.

clue.text: The shift that is seen after dark

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for that is behind the word for dark

parts.note: dark is used as a noun for nightfall or night-time
IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A worker describes the late shift that only begins once darkness falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' reads as a work rota but is an old word for a woman's loose dress or chemise.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple loose dress or slip, and this is one worn in bed.

indicators.note: being in for it means facing trouble, here taken as the letters of so done being knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A captured outlaw is caught and therefore finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for it' rearranges SO DONE; the surface reads as one gloomy sentence, with 'done for' seeming to belong together.
explanation.definitionFit: Noosed means snared in a looped rope, so trapped or captured.

clue.text: Taking a stroll after midnight is taking a risk

indicators.note: after puts the walking word behind the letter from midnight

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
ambling is walking at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Wandering about in the small hours is reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is a crossword convention for the centre letter of NIGHT, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling is betting or speculating, putting something at hazard on chance.

parts.note: lift is slang for steal or pilfer

indicators.note: most of means dropping the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Raise the bulk of the hidden material.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting furtively so as not to be noticed, a kind of concealment.

clue.text: Weather men caught in a flurry of sleet

indicators.note: caught in means the men are trapped within the other letters
a flurry stirs things up, so the letters of sleet whirl into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Forecasters were trapped out in a sleet shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather' looks like a verb but is the noun phrase the weather, as in braving the elements; 'a flurry of' scrambles the snow word to ELETS before the men go in.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements means the forces of nature, wind, rain and cold, as in braving the elements.

annotationWithheld.why: Exhorted to be very topical? (3,3): RED HOT is an anagram of HORTED, the clue word Exhorted with its EX dropped; no separate word signals that removal, so 'Ex' would be both fodder and indicator.

definitions.meaning: a short heavy arrow shot from a crossbow

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crossbow's square-headed arrow and a heated disagreement.

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Send a lady a short line.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to let fall or cast off, as trees do leaves.

clue.text: Fancy coping with bare adults dancing around?

indicators.note: dancing around has the letters of bare adults whirling about into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Naked grown-ups cavorting are wondering how they could possibly cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coping' is not managing but the top course of a wall; a balustrade is a decorative version.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is an ornamental railing of posts topping a balcony or parapet, so a decorative capping.

indicators.note: to disguise is to alter appearance, so the letters of can anyone are rearranged out of recognition

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether irritation can ever be hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance is irritation or displeasure, the feeling of being vexed.

clue.text: Put forward the case against the Euro

parts.note: the case for something is the pro side of an argument
the British pound is the currency championed by those opposed to the single European currency

explanation.surface: A Eurosceptic presents the argument against Britain adopting the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole phrase as 'pro-pound': being for sterling is the case against the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to propose or offer an idea for consideration.

clue.text: Ancient city captured in erudite books

indicators.note: captured in means the city is held inside the word for erudite

parts.note: literate can mean well-read or learned
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An old city is described in scholarly volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is written works collectively, books in general.

parts.note: the phrase means both to strike out with fists and to spend lavishly, which is the remedy for meanness

explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to attack wildly, and also to splash money about freely.

parts.note: S stands for the south pole
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Tie up the old horse to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hitch or unexpected obstacle.

clue.text: Welcome surprise has a divine finish

parts.note: divine is taken as of a god, possessive
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A happy turn of events comes with a heavenly conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of luck that arrives just when needed.

definitions.meaning: a plump game bird of moors

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a game bird of the moors and also a gripe.

definitions.meaning: removes with a ladle or shovel
stories one paper gets before its rivals

explanation.definitionFit: The word means ladles or hollows out, and also newspaper stories printed ahead of competitors.

clue.text: Wild rose one found growing by the river

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild rose has been spotted blooming on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a willow that grows along riverbanks, used for basket-making.

clue.text: It's discharged in battle during action

indicators.note: during places the fight word inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: A gun goes off in the heat of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill defrayed has been paid off, its cost settled.

parts.note: B is second, as in B-grade
a row is a rank or line

explanation.surface: A question of whether to sit in the second row or the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow of a hill is its top edge, and the forehead is the front of the head.

parts.note: deadlines read as lines written about the dead, rather than time limits for copy

explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice of a person's death with an account of their life.

clue.text: Shade of a nun seen round a religious establishment

indicators.note: round means the nun surrounds the single letter a

parts.note: taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A gradation of colour in a nun's habit noticed near a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour.

definitions.meaning: lower the brightness with a switch

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to reject a request, and to lower a light's brightness or volume.

clue.text: Was first to cover the news story

indicators.note: to cover means the first word wraps round the news word

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front
gen is informal British slang for information

explanation.surface: A reporter got in first on the scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, 'the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, often of doubtful truth.
